answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable deposit before it may bid for work. The protocol assigns tasks and checks results, then burns part of the deposit when an agent submits provably invalid work or fails a challenge. Creating a thousand names no longer grants a thousand free chances: each one ties up capital and risks a separate loss. The violet job at the ledge may attract a raven’s many aliases, but those aliases must each pay and remain accountable. This raises the attacker’s cost without claiming to prevent Sybils outright.
